title: Global bond sell-off drives US, Japanese, German yields to multi-decade highs
content:
Government bond yields surged to multi-decade highs across major markets in the week to 4 September 2026. The US 10-year Treasury yield topped **4.82%**, its highest since January 2025, while Japan's 10-year JGB yield reached **3.02%**, a level last seen in 1996, and German Bund and French OAT yields hit their highest since 2011 and 2008 respectively.

Rising oil prices, sticky inflation and mounting bets on a Fed rate hike this month drove the sell-off, which pushed borrowing costs higher globally and weighed on rate-sensitive equities. The synchronised move marks a stark reversal from the ultra-low-yield era and underscores investor concern that inflation, not growth, is now the dominant risk facing major central banks.

title: US payrolls beat forecasts by threefold, reviving Fed hike bets for September
content:
US nonfarm payrolls rose by **162,000** in August, far above the 53,000 forecast and the strongest monthly gain since March, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed on 4 September 2026. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%, in line with expectations, while average hourly earnings rose 3.1% year-on-year; June and July payrolls were revised up by a combined 55,000, adding to signs of underlying labour-market resilience.

The surprise strength pushed fed funds futures-implied odds of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting to roughly **58-65%**, up sharply from around 50% beforehand, while the 2-year UST yield rose and the USD strengthened. Equities fell, led by rate-sensitive growth and technology names, as investors repriced the odds that the Fed's next move could be a hike rather than a cut.

title: Brent nears $97 as US-Iran strikes reignite Strait of Hormuz fears
content:
Brent crude jumped toward **$97/bbl** this week, on track for a roughly 8% weekly gain, after the US carried out fresh strikes against Iran on 1 September 2026, its first such action in about a month, prompting Tehran to retaliate against American bases and vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. WTI crude also rose, briefly topping **$90/bbl**, its highest level in weeks.

The renewed escalation threatens a key artery for global energy supply, through which roughly a quarter of the world's seaborne crude oil normally passes, and adds fresh upside risk to inflation just as central banks weigh their next moves. Higher oil prices have been a key driver of this week's broader sell-off in government bonds and added to pressure on risk assets, with equities and the euro and sterling softening against a firmer dollar.
